$comment: Receipts for every number the viewer displays. Each entry carries the verbatim sentence from the technical report it came from; verify.py enforces that index.html still matches. Numbers the report does not publish are listed under removed_claims and must stay out.

source.title: DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash: Pushing the Limits of KV Cache Compression
source.how_to_recheck: curl -sL -o /tmp/ds41.pdf '<url>' && sha256sum /tmp/ds41.pdf && pdftotext -layout /tmp/ds41.pdf - | grep -i '<quote from this file>'

baseline_source.title: Attention Is All You Need
baseline_source.note: Left tower only: 6+6 layers, d_model 512, 8 heads, d_ff 2048, 65M base / 213M big. The 36 KB/token baseline and the ~41x gap are this project's own arithmetic, not paper numbers, and the UI labels them as such.

claims.claim: Decoder global KV is projected from the final encoder hidden states (H_{L/2}).
claims.value: decoder global KV projected from H₂₀ (the final encoder hidden state)
claims.metric: which hidden state the decoder's global KV comes from, and where the CED boundary is drawn in the built stack
claims.method: index.html builds one stack in code order: 2 SWA blocks, 3x6 CSA2 encoder layers, a 'CED boundary — H₂₀' block, then 5x4 decoder layers whose numbering starts at L20. The check re-derives the encoder layer count from those loop bounds, reads the base index the decoder's layer labels are numbered from, reads the H-index the boundary label names, and requires the boundary block to be constructed between the encoder and decoder groups.
claims.repro: python3 -c 'import re;h=open("index.html",encoding="utf-8").read();D=dict(zip("₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉",range(10)));e=re.findall(r"for \(let g = 0; g < (\d+); g\+\+\) \{\s*for \(let j = 0; j < (\d+); j\+\+\) \{\s*const (?:full|mode)",h);enc=2+int(e[0][0])*int(e[0][1]);base=int(re.search(r"Decoder L\$\{(\d+) \+",h).group(1));hs=int("".join(str(D[c]) for c in re.search(r"H([₀-₉]+)",h).group(1)));i=h.index("const ced = rightBlock");print("encoder L0-L%d"%(enc-1), "decoder base L%d"%base, "CED H%d"%hs, "boundary between stacks:", h.index("const encGroupsLast")<i<h.index("const decBlocks"), "kv from encoder last:", base==enc==hs)'
claims.evidence: index.html (CED boundary block + decoder layer numbering)

source.quote: We adopt a Causal Encoder-Decoder (CED) architecture, in which decoder global KV is projected from the final encoder hidden states.

must_contain: 解码器全局 KV 由编码器最后隐状态投影

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import re;h=open("index.html",encoding="utf-8").read();D=dict(zip("₀₁₂₃₄₅₆₇₈₉",range(10)));e=re.findall(r"for \(let g = 0; g < (\d+); g\+\+\) \{\s*for \(let j = 0; j < (\d+); j\+\+\) \{\s*const (?:full|mode)",h);enc=2+int(e[0][0])*int(e[0][1]);base=int(re.search(r"Decoder L\$\{(\d+) \+",h).group(1));hs=int("".join(str(D[c]) for c in re.search(r"H([₀-₉]+)",h).group(1)));i=h.index("const ced = rightBlock");print("encoder L0-L%d"%(enc-1), "decoder base L%d"%base, "CED H%d"%hs, "boundary between stacks:", h.index("const encGroupsLast")<i<h.index("const decBlocks"), "kv from encoder last:", base==enc==hs)'

expect.equals: encoder L0-L19 decoder base L20 CED H20 boundary between stacks: True kv from encoder last: True

claims.claim: CED computes only the first half of the layers during prefill.
claims.value: prefill = 20 of the 40 layers (half)
claims.metric: encoder layers prefill runs, out of all layers built — in the viewer and in the committed README figure
claims.method: index.html's tower builder fixes the split (2 SWA + 3x6 encoder layers, then 5x4 decoder layers) and the phase toggle dims the decoder's global-attention layers. The committed hero figure assets/readme/hero.svg draws the same stack as 40 layer bars, 20 of them dimmed above the dashed CED boundary, under its own caption 'prefill runs half the stack'. The check derives both counts and requires them to agree.
claims.repro: python3 -c 'import re;h=open("index.html",encoding="utf-8").read();s=int(re.search(r"const swaBlocks = \[\];\s*for \(let i = 0; i < (\d+); i\+\+\)",h).group(1));e=re.findall(r"for \(let g = 0; g < (\d+); g\+\+\) \{\s*for \(let j = 0; j < (\d+); j\+\+\) \{\s*const (?:full|mode)",h);enc=s+int(e[0][0])*int(e[0][1]);tot=enc+int(e[1][0])*int(e[1][1]);v=open("assets/readme/hero.svg",encoding="utf-8").read();bars=re.findall(r"<rect x=.680. y=.[0-9.]+. width=.120. height=.5\.2.[^>]*>",v);print("viewer: prefill %d of %d layers = %s | hero figure: %d of %d layer bars dimmed"%(enc,tot,"half" if enc*2==tot else "NOT half",len([b for b in bars if "opacity" in b]),len(bars)))'

source.quote: This design allows CED to compute only the first half of the layers during the prefill phase

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import re;h=open("index.html",encoding="utf-8").read();s=int(re.search(r"const swaBlocks = \[\];\s*for \(let i = 0; i < (\d+); i\+\+\)",h).group(1));e=re.findall(r"for \(let g = 0; g < (\d+); g\+\+\) \{\s*for \(let j = 0; j < (\d+); j\+\+\) \{\s*const (?:full|mode)",h);enc=s+int(e[0][0])*int(e[0][1]);tot=enc+int(e[1][0])*int(e[1][1]);v=open("assets/readme/hero.svg",encoding="utf-8").read();bars=re.findall(r"<rect x=.680. y=.[0-9.]+. width=.120. height=.5\.2.[^>]*>",v);print("viewer: prefill %d of %d layers = %s | hero figure: %d of %d layer bars dimmed"%(enc,tot,"half" if enc*2==tot else "NOT half",len([b for b in bars if "opacity" in b]),len(bars)))'

claims.claim: Encoder CSA2: 3 groups of 6, first layer Full, next 5 Reuse (m=2).
claims.value: 3 groups x 6 layers, m = 2 — 1 Full + 5 Reuse per group
claims.metric: encoder CSA2 groups, their size, the Full/Reuse split, and the compression rate the blocks carry
claims.method: The encoder group nest in index.html is `for (g < 3) { for (j < 6) { const full = j === 0; ...` and every encoder block sets `b.userData.m = 2`; the check re-derives the group shape, the Full/Reuse counts (3 + 15) and the first userData.m literal.
claims.repro: python3 -c 'import re;h=open("index.html",encoding="utf-8").read();g,j=map(int,re.search(r"for \(let g = 0; g < (\d+); g\+\+\) \{\s*for \(let j = 0; j < (\d+); j\+\+\) \{\s*const full = j === 0;",h).groups());m=int(re.search(r"b\.userData\.m = (\d+);",h).group(1));print("%dx%d groups, %d encoder layers: %d Full + %d Reuse, m=%d"%(g,j,g*j,g,g*(j-1),m))'

source.quote: These layers are divided into three identically configured groups of six layers. In each group, the first layer operates in Full Mode, and the remaining five layers operate in Reuse Mode.

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import re;h=open("index.html",encoding="utf-8").read();g,j=map(int,re.search(r"for \(let g = 0; g < (\d+); g\+\+\) \{\s*for \(let j = 0; j < (\d+); j\+\+\) \{\s*const full = j === 0;",h).groups());m=int(re.search(r"b\.userData\.m = (\d+);",h).group(1));print("%dx%d groups, %d encoder layers: %d Full + %d Reuse, m=%d"%(g,j,g*j,g,g*(j-1),m))'

expect.equals: 3x6 groups, 18 encoder layers: 3 Full + 15 Reuse, m=2

claims.claim: Decoder CSA2: 5 groups of 4, group 1 is Full + 3 Reuse (m=1).
claims.value: 5 groups x 4 layers, m = 1 — group 1 is 1 Full + 3 Reuse
claims.metric: decoder CSA2 groups, their size, the group-1 mode split, and the compression rate
claims.method: The decoder nest in index.html is `for (g < 5) { for (j < 4) { const mode = j === 0 ? (g === 0 ? 'Full' : 'Reindex') : 'Reuse'; ...` with `b.userData.m = 1`; the check re-derives the shape, the group-1 split and the decoder's m literal.

source.quote: The 20 decoder layers use CSA2 with a compression rate of 𝑚 = 1. These layers are divided into five groups of four layers. In the first group, the first layer operates in Full Mode, and the remaining three layers operate in Reuse Mode.

check.cmd: python3 -c 'import re;h=open("index.html",encoding="utf-8").read();g,j=map(int,re.search(r"for \(let g = 0; g < (\d+); g\+\+\) \{\s*for \(let j = 0; j < (\d+); j\+\+\) \{\s*const mode =",h).groups());ms=[int(x) for x in re.findall(r"b\.userData\.m = (\d+);",h)];print("%dx%d groups, %d decoder layers: group 1 = 1 Full + %d Reuse, m=%d"%(g,j,g*j,j-1,ms[1]))'

expect.equals: 5x4 groups, 20 decoder layers: group 1 = 1 Full + 3 Reuse, m=1
